newsitem.title: UK: Prudential fined for breaching PEP rules.
newsitem.headline: Prudential fined for breaching PEP rules.

text.p: British regulator the Investment Mangement Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) said on Monday it had reprimanded and fined Prudential Corp 75,000 pounds for breaching its rules on Personal Equity Plans (PEPs).

At a disciplinary hearing Prudential admitted failing to carry out reconciliations and corrections of PEP client money accounts, failing to notify IMRO of this and failing to have adequate compliance arrangements in place.
Prudential has paid compensation of 25,000 pounds to disadvantaged clients.
The rules broken concerned provisions to ensure companies hold the correct amount of money for clients and are aware of the individual sums of money held for each client at all times.
Prudential said the problems were administrative, involving delays in crediting interest to customers' accounts.

"Prudential very much regrets these problems occurred. When they came to light, remedial action was taken and no customers were disadvantaged. Procedures were put in place to ensure these problems will not occur again," the company said.
